subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw keep the Chrome extension relay retired, restore it as a security-reviewed optional path, or first design a generic browser-backend plugin/API seam for this cross-machine browser-control use case?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses browser-control, signed-in session, remote Gateway, extension, and plugin/API boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term security and product contract.

options.title: Design secure backend API first
options.body: Add a versioned browser backend/plugin contract, then build any relay replacement on top with explicit authorization, tab scope, audit logs, docs, and migration tests.

options.title: Restore relay as optional built-in
options.body: Reintroduce `driver: "extension"` behind an opt-in, security-reviewed path while accepting core ownership of the legacy relay surface.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Document that managed-hosting users must use node hosts, remote CDP, or external relay tooling and keep this issue as the migration-limit record.

recommendation.title: Design secure backend API first
recommendation.body: Add a versioned browser backend/plugin contract, then build any relay replacement on top with explicit authorization, tab scope, audit logs, docs, and migration tests.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the strongest recent history on the browser driver removal and migration surface that triggered the regression.
